title: Python: pin GCLI-144's untested conditions: the lazy-read bindings.length > 0 check and the decorator-site removal (test only)
description: Test-only follow-up from GCLI-144's round 2 (opum-ai/glyph-cli#223, landed 02043cd). Ordinary, not hold. Add fixtures, in a separate PR with no change to src/python/calls.ts, for: (1) N1a: m.py def len; app.py class Outer: type A = len([]); from m import len (head and origin/dev both bin it external 1, no edge); (2) N1b: s.py def f, m.py def f, app.py from s import *; class Outer: type A = f(); from m import f (both give the edge app.py:3:14 to s.py:f); these two pin the 'lazyDiffers && bindings.length > 0' condition in lookupBindings ('unchanged from dev, pre-existing'): the mutant that drops '&& bindings.length > 0' leaves every GCLI-144 fixture green today, changes N1a to nameNotBound 1 and loses N1b's edge, so the fixtures must turn that mutant red; (3) N2: def outer(): def staticmethod(f): return f; class Outer: @staticmethod def m(self): self.n(); def n(self): pass; from m import X as staticmethod (m.py class X): origin/dev has the edge app.py:5:10 to outer.staticmethod, the head removes it (a wrong dev edge: the decorator read goes to the globals and builtins, never the enclosing function), assert the removal and that self.n() keeps its edge. PRE-EXISTING NOTES recorded here, identical on origin/dev, not blockers: N1: a lazy read where Rule 38 dropped the class binding and nothing is bound further out still claims the builtin or the star-supplied name (the N1a and N1b outcomes); N2: isUnshadowedBuiltin and isStarPossiblyBuiltin do not consult classBodyShadowed, so receiver edges survive where a builtin test is made through them. Not started.

acceptanceCriteria.text: N1a and N1b fixtures measured against origin/dev and the head by running both (identical), and the mutant that drops bindings.length > 0 observed red on them
The N2 fixture asserts the removed decorator-site edge and the surviving self.n() edge, red on origin/dev, green at the head
No change to src/python/calls.ts; five-pin cmp identical
